articles.title: Buffalo Bills depth chart: Projected starting lineup vs. Texans
articles.summary: The Bills' first depth chart shows a familiar offense around Josh Allen and a revamped defense under new coordinator Jim Leonhard.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills changed head coaches for the first time in nearly a decade.

Josh Allen might barely notice when he looks around the huddle.

The other side of the ball is a different story.

Buffalo released its first unofficial depth chart ahead of Sunday's season opener against the Houston Texans , giving the clearest look yet at how Joe Brady's first starting lineup could look.

The offense is mostly familiar. The defense is not.

Only two starters on offense are different from Buffalo's opening depth chart last season. The Bills could have more than twice that many changes on defense as coordinator Jim Leonhard installs a new 3-4 scheme.

The Bills visit the Texans at 1 p.m. Sunday, Sept. 13, at Reliant Stadium.

Here's a look at Buffalo's projected starting lineup, what's changed from last season and the complete depth chart.

Buffalo Bills projected starting offense vs. Texans

There are two changes to the Bills' offensive starters from a year ago.

WR: DJ Moore — The biggest change among Buffalo's skill-position starters. The Bills traded with the Chicago Bears for Moore during the offseason.

LG: Alec Anderson — Won the starting job over Austin Corbett in training camp.

Buffalo Bills projected starting defense vs. Texans

The first thing that looks different is the formation.

Buffalo is listed in a base 3-4 defense under Leonhard after playing primarily out of a four-man defensive front under Sean McDermott.

That makes a direct position-by-position comparison imperfect, but the personnel turnover is obvious.

DL: T.J. Sanders — Moves into a prominent role after being part of Buffalo's defensive tackle rotation as a rookie. He's listed as one of three starting defensive linemen.

DL: Deone Walker — Takes over in the middle of the defensive front. DaQuan Jones occupied that role in Buffalo's old defense entering last season.

OLB: Bradley Chubb — One of Buffalo's biggest offseason changes. Chubb signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract and replaces Joey Bosa as the veteran pass rusher opposite Rousseau.

LB: Dorian Williams — Steps into a full-time starting role after Matt Milano opened last season alongside Bernard.

CB: Maxwell Hairston — Listed as the starter opposite Benford after beginning his rookie season on injured reserve last year.

NB: Dee Alford — Signed a three-year, $15.75 million free-agent contract to take over the nickel job previously held by Taron Johnson . The Bills traded Johnson during the offseason.

FS: C.J. Gardner-Johnson — Replaces Taylor Rapp and gives Buffalo another veteran addition to a secondary that changed substantially during the offseason.

Buffalo Bills projected special teams starters

P/H: Tommy Doman Jr. — The Bills' rookie seventh-round pick beat out veteran Mitch Wishnowsky for the job.

PR: Dee Alford — His spot atop the punt-returner depth chart is one of the more surprising details in Buffalo's first release.

The depth chart is unofficial and injuries could still alter Buffalo's actual Week 1 lineup.

C: Connor McGovern; Lloyd Cushenberry III

RG: O'Cyrus Torrence; Ar'maj Reed-Adams; Austin Corbett

DE: T.J. Sanders; Landon Jackson ; Phidarian Mathis (suspended)

DE: Ed Oliver; DeWayne Carter ; Zane Durant (IR)

OLB: Greg Rousseau; Michael Hoecht ; Mike Danna

OLB: Bradley Chubb; TJ Parker; Javon Solomon

S: C.J. Gardner-Johnson; Damar Hamlin ; Sam Franklin Jr.

articles.title: 'Outstanding' star makes Liverpool hierarchy eat their words about his future
articles.summary: Liverpool have made a lot of changes to their squad this summer. Some players such as Harvey Elliott and Curtis Jones have been moved on, while others, such...
articles.body:
Liverpool have made a lot of changes to their squad this summer.

Some players such as Harvey Elliott and Curtis Jones have been moved on , while others, such as Victor Munoz and Jeremy Jacquet have been brought in.

It's not just their playing staff what have changed either with a decent chunk of the Reds' backroom staff also being re-jigged.

Richard Hughes is now Al-Hilal's sporting director and Michael Edwards just decided to quit after Fenway Sports Group's multi-club model was thrown in the bin.

Even though all these changes have been made, it still feels like more needs to be done before Liverpool are ready to be seen as genuine contenders for the Premier League title again.

And, with the sheer number of contracts that are set to expire over the next couple of years, it's clear that a lot more re-jigging is on its way to Anfield.

However, for one Liverpool star, it feels like he's made a mockery of Liverpool after the decision that they made about his future.

Alexis Mac Allister has been told that he isn't good enough for a new Liverpool contract

Alexis Mac Allister 's contract may not expire until 2028 but, with the way that things have gone for Liverpool over the last couple of years, locking down the future's of any players with any sort of value is going to be key to their survival.

Recently, Trent Alexander-Arnold , Ibrahima Konate, Mohamed Salah and Andy Robertson have all left L4 for nothing.

Obviously, some players such as Robertson and Salah may not have had all that much value left within them but, it still sucks for the Reds to have lost them for nothing.

And, since Jones' contract was going to expire at the end of the current campaign, he was also moved on for a cut-rate fee.

This is a pattern that Liverpool can't continue to follow but, as per an update from BBC Sport, it seems like Liverpool didn't think that Mac Allister was anywhere near good enough to earn a new contract.

"The understanding is the powers that be at Liverpool were of the belief that Mac Allister's performances did not warrant the offer of fresh terms," they wrote .

"But if he can carry on like this, then it will be a question of when rather than if that offer is made for whoever replaces Richard Hughes - even if Mac Allister said he didn't know if his goal would boost his chances of a new contract."

Alexis Mac Allister has already proven that Liverpool are wrong about their assumptions

Over the last few weeks, it's clear that Andoni Iraola has been trying to figure out what his best XI actually is.

Cody Gakpo has been used on the right-wing and, the Reds' midfield has been changed around more times than anyone can remember.

From an outside perspective, it felt obvious that Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch would be Liverpool's starting midfielders.

However, after their opening game as a pair against Newcastle, it was clear that it wasn't going to work out.

So, this has led to Mac Allister being given a more prominent role than anyone expected and, if we're being honest, he's exceeded the expectations of everyone.

Last term, the Argentinian performed well below his usual standards with fans even demanding that he got sold.

However, that didn't end up happening which is why it's now a bit of a shock to see him becoming one of Liverpool's best players.

His determination on the pitch has been second-to-none and, his goal against Atletico Madrid on Wednesday evening was stunning.

If he continues performing to this level, he'll certainly end up making Liverpool re-think their stance on the " outstanding " midfielders future, even if a renewal is likely to cost them an arm and a leg.

articles.title: Explained: Is cricket a designated sport under National Sports Governance Act? Will NSGA bring BCCI under RTI?
articles.summary: More sports News: Earlier this week, the Supreme Court asked the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and its state associations to clarify their position on th.
articles.body: Earlier this week, the Supreme Court asked the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) and its state associations to clarify their position on the National Sports Governance Act (NSGA) after multiple litigations involving state cricket associations either for minor changes in their constitution, or disputes arising from factionalism over control of the bodies.A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana asked the BCCI and state associations to explain why the terms and conditions of service of their office-bearers should not be governed by the NSGA.The BCCI had argued that the NSGA doesn't apply to them. “...even though the National Sports Governance Act 2025 has been enacted, the sport of cricket has not been notified as a designated sport for the National Sports Governance Act to apply,” the BCCI had said in an affidavit before the Odisha High Court in a case relating to the election of the Odisha Cricket Association (OCA) office-bearers.The BCCI urged the OCA to conduct their elections or risk having its funds withheld and being derecognised. The OCA, in reply, argued that the elections have only been deferred to assess the impact of the NSGA, especially now that cricket is an Olympic sport.All these back and forth beg the most basic question: Does BCCI come under the NSGA? What is a 'designated sport'? If cricket does come under the NSGA, does it also come under the RTI? TimesofIndia.com asked Aahna Mehrotra, founder of AM Sports Law & Management Co., to explain these, and more, questions.Q. What does “designated sport” mean under the NSGA, and who decides which sports get notified?Under the Act, a “designated sport” is any sport discipline that the Central Government, by notification, specifies to be a designated sport, whether for a particular region or State or for the whole of India. The decision is thus an executive act of the Central Government, through the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports. This matters because the core architecture of sport is a pyramidal structure wherein there must be one National Sports Federation (NSF) for each designated sport, and it is this designation that draws a sport, and its federation, into the recognition and oversight of the National Sports Board (NSB) and the jurisdiction of the National Sports Tribunal (NST).Q. Why hasn’t cricket been notified as a designated sport, and can the government notify it later?The Act has been brought into force in stages starting January 2026, but no sport has yet been notified as a designated sport, cricket included. The rollout seems deliberately sequenced, with the machinery of the Board and the Tribunal being made operational before individual sports are brought in. The fact that the BCCI takes no central government funding places it in a distinctive position. A comparison of the draft Bill tabled in Parliament in July 2025 with the Act as passed in August 2025 reveals a telling change in the structuring of Sections 14 and 15.Act:14. (1) Only a recognised sports organisation shall be eligible to receive grants or any other financial assistance from the Central Government.(2) A recognised sports organisation, receiving grants or any other financial assistance from the Central Government under sub-section (1) or from a State Government, shall be considered as a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005, with respect to utilisation of such grants or any other financial assistance.15. A recognised sports organisation shall ensure that all its voting members and affiliate units, as applicable, complies with—(a) the International Charters and Statutes, as applicable, and shall exercise the rights, perform the duties and discharge the functions as specified therein; and(b) the provisions of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder.Bill:14. Only a recognised sports organisation shall be eligible to receive grants or any other financial assistance from the Central Government.15. (1) A recognised sports organisation shall ensure that all its voting members and affiliate units, as applicable, complies with— (a) the International Charters and Statutes, as applicable, and shall exercise the rights, perform the duties and discharge the functions as specified therein; and(b) the provisions of this Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder.(2) A recognised sports organisation shall be considered as a public authority under the Right to Information Act, 2005 with respect to the exercise of its functions, duties and powers under this ActWhat the final Act made central, therefore, is the receiving of grants or financial assistance. On the strength of other provisions, for instance Section 27 on the use of national names and insignia, the BCCI may have to comply with the Act to some extent even now. But until cricket is notified as a designated sport, it is not under the Act. My reading, for the present, is this: although the Act supersedes the National Sports Development Code, 2011, the transition is not yet complete, and until sports are designated and the new framework is fully in operation, the 2011 Code will continue to apply in some measure, as the Ministry’s suspension of the Table Tennis Federation of India (TTFI) in August 2026 showed, an order issued expressly under the powers conferred by the 2011 Code. In any event, the BCCI was never governed by the Code; it operated under the 2014 Supreme Court judgment and is governed by a Supreme Court-approved constitution. More than anything else, I expect cricket’s inclusion at the 2028 Olympic Games to be the trigger that finally makes it a designated sport and brings the BCCI in as a National Sports Federation, though even then it will not fall under the Right to Information Act (RTI) unless it takes government funding.The designation of sports is not a one-time window: the Central Government may notify cricket at any time by a fresh notification.The question has now acquired an apex-level dimension. In its order of 9 September 2026 the Supreme Court asked the BCCI and the state associations to show why they should not be governed by the Act, which suggests that cricket’s entry into the statutory regime may be driven as much by the Court as by a government notification, and possibly sooner than the phased rollout alone would have implied.Q. If cricket isn’t designated, does the National Sports Board have any authority over BCCI at all right now?As things stand, essentially no. The recognition and regulatory powers of the National Sports Board, and the obligations that attach to a National Sports Federation, such as bringing byelaws into conformity within six months, constituting athletes’ committees, and submitting to election oversight and Tribunal jurisdiction, all largely attach to federations for designated sports. Until cricket is designated and the BCCI is recognised as its federation, the BCCI is not a National Sports Body under the Act, and the Board has no recognition or oversight hold over it. A few provisions of general application may still be relevant, such as the control over the use of “India”, “National” and national insignia, but the BCCI’s governance is presently anchored not in the National Sports Board but in its Supreme Court-approved constitution and the Court’s continuing directions.Q. Does the NSGA override the Lodha Committee reforms, or do the two coexist?The Justice Lodha-derived constitution, mandated and approved by the Supreme Court in its 2018 and 2022 orders, governs the BCCI and its state units on its own footing. Once cricket is designated, the two regimes would overlap on some counts, but they would also diverge on certain points. Where they diverge, the position is unsettled for now, but my sense is that the Supreme Court would eventually require the BCCI to fall in line with the lay of the land.The question is no longer merely academic. As noted above, the Supreme Court has now asked the BCCI and the state associations why they should not be governed by the Act. What matters here is the implication: the very court that authored the Lodha framework is itself weighing whether to hand cricket over to the statutory regime. If it does, the coexistence question may be resolved not by a contest between the two frameworks but by the Court itself transitioning cricket from its own supervision to the Act, which would be the most authoritative way the precedence issue could be settled.Q. Is BCCI’s argument, that the NSGA doesn’t apply but its Supreme Court-mandated constitution does, legally consistent, or is it picking convenient parts of two frameworks?It is legally consistent, and not, on a fair reading, cherry-picking, because the two frameworks have different trigger conditions. The Act applies to designated sports; cricket is so far not one, so by the statute’s own terms it does not yet bind the BCCI. The Supreme Court-approved constitution binds the BCCI and its members by force of the Court’s orders, independently of the Act. The Board is therefore not selecting convenient parts of two live regimes; it is pointing out that one regime has not been enforced upon cricket, while the other is in force and unaffected. That the two happen to point the same way here, namely that elections must be held, does not make the position incoherent.Critics may say the optics are convenient, and that the Board is content to keep the statutory oversight at bay while embracing the reform elements that reinforce central control over the states. But that is an argument about motive and appearance, not legal consistency. On the law, the designated-sport point is correct.This stance is, however, now being tested at the highest level. The Court’s query is a clear signal that the gap the BCCI is relying on may not stay open for long.Q. Does BCCI’s continued RTI exemption survive the NSGA, or is that a separate legal question?It is a separate question, and the exemption survives the Act on two independent footings. The Act, as enacted, narrowed the transparency provision so that a recognised sports body is a public authority under the Right to Information Act only in respect of its utilisation of government grants or other financial assistance. Since the BCCI takes no government grants, the Act does not bring it within the Right to Information Act at all. Independently of the Act, the Central Information Commission held in May 2026 that the BCCI is not a “public authority” under Section 2(h) of the Right to Information Act 2005, being neither created by law nor owned, controlled or substantially financed by the Government, a ruling that followed the setting aside of the earlier 2018 Commission order. So the BCCI remains outside the Right to Information regime on grounds that do not depend on the designation question, though it remains answerable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226 for its public functions. Designating cricket would not, by itself, place the BCCI under the Right to Information Act unless it began to take government grants.BCCI remains outside the Right to Information regime on grounds that do not depend on the designation question, though it remains answerable to writ jurisdiction under Article 226 for its public functionsQ. Can a state association cite a Central Act (NSGA) to override its national federation’s (BCCI’s) own byelaws on elections?Not in the way the Odisha Cricket Association is presently attempting to. While cricket is undesignated, the Act does not apply to it, so there is no operative statutory provision for the OCA to set against the BCCI Constitution. And even after the Act applies, a state unit could not use it to override the Supreme Court-approved constitution and the Court’s binding directions, because the Act would operate through the National Sports Board and federation structure, not as a self-executing shield that lets a member defy both its federation and the Court. The order of authority is that the Supreme Court’s directions and the approved constitution sit above the OCA’s byelaws, and the Act is not yet in the cricket picture at all. A Central Act can displace subordinate byelaws where it applies and occupies the field, but here it neither applies to cricket yet nor licenses defiance of binding Supreme Court orders, so the OCA cannot lawfully rely on it to defer polls that its own byelaws and the Court’s mandate require.That said, a separate debate may be inevitable over whether the Act can be applied to state associations at all, given that sport is a State subject under Entry 33 of the State List. This tension was hinted at during the AIFF matter before the Supreme Court. It echoes the federalism question now before the Supreme Court in the challenge to the Promotion and Regulation of Online Gaming Act, 2025, though the parallel is inexact: betting and gambling is a long-settled State subject with decades of jurisprudence behind it, whereas the constitutional footing of a sports-governance statute is far less charted. In any event, the Act reaches state associations only indirectly, through the national federation's duty to secure their compliance rather than by direct central command. Either way, the National Sports Federations hold a practical lever: they are free to frame their byelaws to admit only those state bodies that comply with the federation’s constitution, so a non-compliant state that tries to override the structure risks being expelled from the pyramid altogether.The designation of sports is not a one-time window. The Central Government may notify cricket at any time by a fresh notificationQ. Does a Sports Ministry “notice” carry statutory force if cricket isn’t a designated sport?A ministry communication, advisory or “notice” is executive in character, not statutory. Under the Act, statutory force attaches to notifications made under it, such as one designating a sport or notifying Rules. If cricket is not a designated sport, a ministry notice, whether it urges elections under the Act or is said to permit deferral to a later date, carries no statutory force either to compel or to excuse, and cannot override the Supreme Court-approved constitution or the Court’s binding directions. This is borne out by the Ministry’s own stated position that, pending notification of the Rules, elections could proceed under the Supreme Court-approved framework, which shows that the Ministry itself does not treat the Act as presently binding on cricket. Absent designation and a notification under the Act, a ministry notice is persuasive at most, not law.Q. Could other BCCI state units (beyond OCA) now use the same “wait for NSGA clarity” argument to stall elections?That is the real risk, and it is precisely why the BCCI is pressing the OCA to hold its polls. If deferral on a “wait for the Act, or for the Board’s circular” basis were allowed to succeed, other state units whose incumbents are approaching the two-consecutive-term, cooling-off and nine-year limits could copy the tactic to entrench themselves. But the argument is legally weak while cricket is undesignated, and there is contrary precedent within cricket itself. During the Lodha implementation the Supreme Court’s Committee of Administrators compelled state elections and warned non-compliant units, such as Tamil Nadu and Haryana, with the loss of BCCI voting rights, and states like Maharashtra and Karnataka have held their elections under the Lodha framework. The petitioner has made exactly that point.The recent Supreme Court development cuts against the stalling rather than for it. Its evident impatience with the unending litigation, and its interest in moving these disputes to the National Sports Tribunal, signal a push towards finality. A show-cause on whether the Act should apply does not suspend the existing Supreme Court-approved constitution, and incumbents cannot treat the mere pendency of that question as a licence to defer. If anything, the apex court’s engagement makes an early and uniform resolution more likely, which is the opposite of what a stalling unit would want.Q. What would meaningfully resolve this ambiguity: a formal notification, a Sports Ministry clarification, or judicial intervention?The three are best seen as complementary rather than as alternatives, each operating at a different level:a.A formal notification designating cricket, with the BCCI’s recognition as the federation and the byelaw conformity that follows, would bring cricket under the Act’s ambit and end the “not a designated sport” argument at a stroke. It is the cleanest structural fix, though it then raises the reconciliation with the Lodha framework discussed earlier.b.A Sports Ministry clarification could give administrative guidance, for instance confirming that, pending designation, associations must continue to follow the Supreme Court-approved constitution. It would help set expectations but lacks statutory force and cannot bind a court or settle the legal question.c.Judicial intervention is what will actually resolve the present impasse and, ultimately, the question of precedence. Only a court can enforce the Supreme Court mandate against a unit that will not act, and adjudicate any conflict between the Act and the approved constitution, with the Supreme Court the ultimate forum given its continuing oversight of the BCCI reforms.The events of 9 September 2026 have, in effect, answered this question in favour of judicial intervention, and at the highest level. With the Supreme Court now seized of whether cricket should come under the Act, a direction from it could resolve both the immediate impasse and the precedence question in a single stroke, and could either prompt or make redundant a separate government designation. So while a formal notification remains the cleanest structural route and a ministry clarification the weakest, the operative resolver has now plainly become the judiciary, and specifically the Supreme Court.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ayumi Leiva, oro en el Grand Slam de Budapest
articles.standfirst: La española logra su séptima medalla en un Grand Slam y es la primera vez que sube a lo más alto del podio
articles.summary: La española logra su séptima medalla en un Grand Slam y es la primera vez que sube a lo más alto del podio
articles.body: Ayumi Leiva se marcha del Grand Slam de Budapest con el oro en -52kg tras ganar en la final a la polaca Barbara Twarowska. Es su séptima medalla en una competición de este nivel, pero la primera vez que logra la victoria final. Antes había logrado dos platas (Astaná y Tashkent en 2025) y cuatro bronces (Bakú y París en 2025 y Astaná y Antalya en 2024). Leiva, campeona de Europa sub 23 en 2024, logró un yuko con un o-uchi-gari gracias a un agarre al final de la manga, la española controló el resto del combate e incluso obligó a su rival a recibir una penalización. Con este oro se desquitó de su anterior actuación en el Grand Slam de Suiza donde se despidió en su primer combate. En este 2026 había sido tercera en los Grand Prix de Austria y de Qingdao. "Tras esa dura derrota en Suiza, venir a Budapest fue sin duda la decisión correcta. Mi entrenador siempre me recuerda que necesito una verdadera ambición por ganar, y esa agresividad marcó la diferencia. Estoy muy orgullosa de haber conseguido mi primera medalla de oro en un Grand Slam y profundamente agradecida a mis entrenadores en Valencia por su apoyo incondicional", comentó tras la final. En su camino hasta la lucha por el oro, venció en octavos a la italiana Kena Perna con un yuko. Luego se impuso a la rusa Lilia Nugaeva por ippon. En semifinales, también con un ippon, se llevó el combate ante la neerlandesa Naomi Van Krevel.

articles.title: El CSD da un paso más en la protección de la maternidad con un programa de ayudas de 700.000 euros
articles.standfirst: Pretende favorecer la conciliación e incorpora por primera vez ayudas específicas para la gestación segura, el postparto y la reincorporación progresiva al entrenamiento y la competición.
articles.summary: Pretende favorecer la concialiación e incorpora por primera vez ayudas específicas para la gestación segura, el postparto y la reincorporación progresiva al entrenamiento y la competición.
articles.body: La maternidad no debería ser la línea de meta de ninguna carrera deportiva. El Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD) quiere convertir esa idea en una realidad y ha dado un paso adelante con una nueva convocatoria de ayudas sociales que eleva hasta los 700.000 euros la dotación destinada a favorecer la conciliación de la vida familiar, académica y profesional de las mujeres en el deporte. Son 250.000 euros más que en 2025, un incremento del 55%. La principal novedad está en la creación de una línea específica para acompañar a las deportistas durante el embarazo, el postparto y su regreso progresivo a los entrenamientos y a la competición. El objetivo es evitar que ser madre obligue a aparcar una trayectoria deportiva o a retrasar una decisión personal por miedo a las consecuencias sobre la carrera profesional. “La maternidad no puede convertirse en un obstáculo para la carrera de una deportista ni para la permanencia de una mujer en el deporte. Así, el CSD da un paso adelante para que la conciliación deje de ser una responsabilidad individual de las mujeres y pase a ser también una responsabilidad de las instituciones deportivas y de los poderes públicos”, comenta José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes, presidente del CSD. La convocatoria, publicada este sábado 12 de septiembre en el Boletín Oficial del Estado (BOE), pretende corregir las dificultades que todavía afrontan las mujeres en el deporte profesional, según señala el CSD en un comunicado. Especialmente, las asociadas al retorno a la actividad después de la maternidad y al poder compatibilizar la vida familiar y deportiva. La ayuda para la gestación segura y la reincorporación progresiva podrá alcanzar los 6.200 euros por beneficiaria. Incluye atención ginecológica y obstétrica, fisioterapia especializada, apoyo psicológico, preparación física adaptada, readaptación físico-deportiva, asesoramiento nutricional, asistencia de matrona y asesoramiento en lactancia y salud mamaria. El itinerario de servicios podrá desarrollarse durante el embarazo y hasta doce meses después del parto. El respaldo no se limita a la ayuda económica. El CSD pone también a disposición de las beneficiarias la nueva Unidad de Salud de la Mujer Deportista del Centro de Medicina de Alto Rendimiento del CAR de Madrid. Ofrecerá consultas presenciales o telemáticas, tanto iniciales como de seguimiento, además de las derivaciones que sean necesarias, de forma gratuita. La convocatoria refuerza las ayudas vinculadas directamente a la maternidad. Las beneficiarias podrán recibir hasta 3.500 euros por nacimiento, adopción, guarda con fines de adopción o acogimiento producido durante 2025. A ello se suman hasta 3.500 euros anuales por cada persona a cargo para facilitar la conciliación de la vida deportiva y familiar. Estas cantidades pueden destinarse al cuidado de menores de tres años, de hijos con una discapacidad reconocida igual o superior al 33% hasta los 18 años y de familiares de hasta segundo grado en situación de dependencia. Otra de las novedades es la ampliación de los colectivos que pueden acceder a estas ayudas. Ya no se dirigen únicamente a deportistas de alto nivel y alto rendimiento: también alcanzan a técnicas, entrenadoras, árbitras y juezas. "El objetivo es que la igualdad no se limite al terreno de juego. La presencia de mujeres sigue siendo insuficiente en los espacios técnicos, de entrenamiento y arbitrales, especialmente en los niveles superiores. La convocatoria reconoce que las barreras asociadas a la maternidad y la conciliación afectan también a estas profesionales y busca favorecer su promoción y consolidar referentes femeninos en todos los ámbitos del deporte”, ha indicado Rodríguez Uribes. Las nuevas ayudas serán, además, compatibles con las Becas Maternidad del programa CSD Team España-ADO. Las deportistas beneficiarias de estas becas tienen garantizado el mantenimiento del apoyo económico durante los dos años posteriores al nacimiento, de forma decreciente, para facilitar el periodo de maternidad y el regreso a la competición. La convocatoria contempla también hasta 3.500 euros por solicitud para formación deportiva, destinados a estudios oficiales relacionados con el ámbito profesional del deporte, desde enseñanzas deportivas y ciclos de Actividades Físicas y Deportivas hasta determinados grados universitarios, másteres y programas de doctorado. Las deportistas interesadas en estas ayudas disponen de 10 días hábiles desde el día siguiente a la publicación de la convocatoria en el Boletín Oficial del Estado para presentar sus solicitudes a través de la Sede Electrónica del CSD.

articles.title: Two men receive jail terms for violent burglary of Man City’s Donnarumma
articles.summary: Two men jailed after Italy international Gianluigi Donnarumma and his now wife attacked in Paris home during PSG stint.
articles.body:
Two men involved in a violent burglary of Manchester City’s Italy international goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend at their home in Paris have been given prison sentences.

Donnarumma was savagely beaten in the robbery while his then fiancee, now wife, Alessia Elefante, was choked with a cable and later suffered a miscarriage blamed on the trauma of the incident.

Ilyas Kherbouch, 21, the mastermind of the burglary, was sentenced to nine years in prison and fined 80,000 euros ($93,000) by the Paris Criminal Court.

Co-defendant Moktar D received a five-year prison sentence, with two years suspended subject to a probationary period.

A third defendant, Khyan M, whom prosecutors suspected of also orchestrating the robbery from his prison cell, was acquitted.

The 27-year-old Donnarumma and his partner Elefante were bound and threatened at knifepoint during the terrifying ordeal in their luxury apartment on Avenue Montaigne in central Paris in July 2023, a court in the French capital heard.

At the time of the burglary, the Italian international was playing for Paris Saint-Germain. He moved to Manchester City in 2025.

Prosecutors had requested prison sentences ranging from four to 10 years against the three men alleged to have orchestrated or participated in the violent burglary.

The harshest sentence of 10 years had been sought for Kherbouch, alias “Ganito” – who gained notoriety following his brazen escape from Villepinte prison in Seine-Saint-Denis, north of Paris last March.

Prosecutors requested sentences of nine years and six years respectively for Khyan M, 22, known as “Kiki”, who, like Kherbouch, had been suspected of having orchestrated the violent burglary from his prison cell, and Moktar D, one of the robbers.

In the early hours of July 21, 2023, Donnarumma and his fiancee were dragged from their bed and held captive by four masked men who had broken into their luxury ninth-floor apartment via the rooftops.

Donnarumma was beaten with hard knuckle gloves until he bled. “The money, the watches!” their attackers roared. Elefante was choked with a phone charging cable, and the couple were separated and tied up.

A seven-man gang – some of whom remain unidentified – made off in minutes with cash, jewellery, watches and luxury bags, whose worth the Italian footballer estimated at just less than one million euros ($1.1m).

The exclusive Avenue Montaigne neighbourhood has been “targeted by an increasingly youthful criminal population”, the prosecutor noted during his closing arguments, listing seven celebrities who had fallen victim between 2022 and 2025.

It is a form of crime that is “highly lucrative” and “extremely violent”, targeting “its own idols”, the prosecution added.

The second and final day of this high-profile trial unfolded calmly, with Kherbouch apologising to the police officers he had insulted on Thursday, as well as to the court.

The two alleged masterminds behind the operation denied any involvement during questioning, despite messages and images recovered from phones they had been using while in custody.

Moktar D, the only defendant present at the scene of the burglary, claimed he had merely acted as a lookout, positioned atop a building opposite the couple’s apartment.

His childhood friend, also implicated in the case and accused of being an informant, committed suicide in prison.

articles.body: Indian wushu player Divyanshi Choudhary was looking forward to making her Asian Games debut in Nagoya. However, just days before the event, the 18-year-old was dropped from the Indian squad.Divyanshi had been sharing her excitement on social media as the Games approached. She posted pictures of her kit and also shared moments from the Indian team’s send-off ceremony in New Delhi.Her latest video, however, showed a very different side. Standing on the roof of her hostel at the National Institute of Sports in Patiala, Divyanshi was seen in tears as she spoke about being left out of the team.She said she was removed from the women’s 60kg category and replaced by Roshibina Devi Naorem, whom she had beaten in the selection trials.“I’m tired of this... I have been mentally harassed so much. Since June, July, they have been after me because she (Roshibina) wanted to go. Given that I beat her, why is it a problem for her now,” Divyanshi said in the video.“I beat her, it’s my right to go there (Japan). She has been knocking at different doors...it’s abuse of power,” she added.Father questions last-minute decisionDivyanshi’s father, Sunil, said the family was informed about the decision only on Friday morning. He claimed that they were not given any reason for her removal.He also alleged that Divyanshi was supposed to be told about the decision only after reaching the airport, when she would have been informed that she was not travelling with the team.Sunil also questioned the decision to replace Divyanshi with Roshibina, a world medallist, two-time Asian medallist and Arjuna awardee.“Divyanshi beat Roshibina in the semifinals of the trials. If the association had to send someone, they should have sent the individual who Divyanshi beat in the final,” Sunil told Sportstar.ID@undefined Caption not available.What Wushu body saidThe Wushu Association of India has rejected the allegations. Its president Jitender Bajwa said the federation was not responsible for removing Divyanshi from the squad.Bajwa said the Sports Authority of India (SAI) took the decision after an injury was discovered.“Divyanshi joined the national camp which was organised by SAI a month back. She was carrying a knee injury and was trying to hide it by avoiding training. When SAI eventually found out about this, the replaced her name,” Bajwa told Sportstar.Divyanshi’s father admitted that she had suffered an injury but said she was undergoing treatment.“After she got an injury, we got Divyanshi checked by a doctor. She had an injury to her ACL (Anterior Cruiciate ligament). The doctor said it could be treated by rehabilitation,” Sunil said.Federation explains Roshibina’s selectionBajwa said the coaches at the national camp noticed that Divyanshi was not training and recommended that she undergo a medical examination.“The coaches in the camp had recommended that Divyanshi be checked for an injury because she was not training. Eventually, the coaches informed SAI which arranged for a medical test which showed she was carrying a knee injury. They couldn’t carry an injured athlete to the Asian Games so they had to remove her name,” he said.Bajwa also explained why Roshibina was chosen despite losing to Divyanshi in the selection trials.He said Himanshi of Chandigarh, who lost in the final, had suffered a jaw fracture and was therefore unavailable as a replacement.“The losing finalist, Himanshi of Chandigarh, suffered a fracture to her jaw which is why her name was not included. Instead the coaches had already recommended the name of Roshibina Devi as the replacement player for Divyanshi,” Bajwa said.Bajwa said the federation was also disappointed that Divyanshi would miss the Asian Games.“She is a very talented athlete. She performed very well at the trials. It is bad luck that she will not be going to the Asian Games,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: BS Meter on WWE Stars to AEW Rumors, Backstage Raw Drama, Cody Rhodes' Heel Turn, More
articles.summary: It's blink-and-miss-it season on the pro wrestling rumor mill.
articles.body:
It's blink-and-miss-it season on the pro wrestling rumor mill.

Sure, the WWE calendar might not have anything major in the PLE department and WrestleMania season isn't exactly close.

But recent weeks on the rumor mill have been spot on with major items like the New Level in AEW, Bronson Reed's return and so much more.

It feels like the mill is trying to one-up itself by the week, too. This time out, we've got major buzz on Cody Rhodes, company-hopping speculation for wrestlers and major upcoming plans, to name a few things.

To help fans keep up with the wild rumor mill, let's place the must-know rumors on the BS Meter, with 10 being the highest form of unbelievable buzz fans can safely dismiss.

Is Cody Rhodes finally a bad guy? Maybe not. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats), vicious actions by Rhodes against Randy Orton recently are not a sign of things to come for him as a heel.

Rhodes certainly hinted at some heelish things during his match with Orton at Sunday Night's Main Event. And it's not even close to the first time he's hinted at making a full-blown turn.

Call it 50-50. Rhodes pretty infamously didn't seem to want to go heel in AEW. But his WWE run has had plenty of hints at doing just that. Maybe they're really slow-burning it this time and will save the full turn for an even bigger event. Might as well invest in the long-term story some more at this point, right?

So much for Bayley going to AEW. According to Fightful (h/t Mrosko ), Bayley's recent WWE return doesn't necessarily mean that AEW is giving up hope because, prior to the return, they had hopes to make a play for her in free agency.

Bayley was doing a really good job of drumming up buzz for herself by hinting at a change recently. But her return to Raw recently would seemingly shut down anything about going to AEW, for better or worse.

Of course AEW had an interest in Bayley for a very long list of reasons that would keep us locked here for far too long. It's hard to imagine, from a very basic business perspective, though, that she reappeared on WWE television without a new deal.

Elsewhere on the AEW-pursuing-wrestlers front, according to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp (h/t Cain A. Knight of Cageside Seats), the promotion had talks with Kairi Sane, but it was never realistic for her to join before last month's All In.

The report even goes on to mention that there is "nothing imminent" on this topic. That shuts down plenty of (fair) fan sentiment that Sane going to AEW was a mere matter of time, given the fit.

Everything looks good here. We can't know the particulars of what Sane wants on her next deal or otherwise. But it's blatantly obvious that she's a massive international free agent who can take all the time she wants to make her pick of the many promotions undoubtedly after her.

WWE has four major PLEs left and a smattering of other things. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ), the promotion has put Worlds Collide at 8 p.m. ET to "directly compete" with AEW's All Out.

No shocker here, as this is WWE habit by now. Also, of note, is Wrestle Inc's Nishant Jayaram citing the same report as 6 p.m. ET starts for Money in the Bank and Survivor Series: WarGames. Crown Jewel is set for 1 p.m. ET and WrestlePalooza, from Perth, Australia, will start at 6 a.m. ET.

Times always subject to change, of course. One thing that isn't? WWE insisting on acting like AEW isn't direct competition while also making sure to counter-program it. Propping up smaller brands to directly compete, too, is a very WWE thing to do, for better or worse.

Here comes Disney chatter. According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ),WWE has plans to hopefully use ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex in Orlando for brand awareness events, plus hopes that wrestlers can actually make it onto some sort of Disney+ programming.

Let this report tell it, WWE has desired a Disney connect before the ESPN deal even came together. No matter what happens with ESPN moving forward, one would presume that stance won't change.

Easiest buy of the week, really. Of course WWE wants to expand into as many avenues as it can, never mind one as big as Disney. We'll see how serious things get, but it's an obvious way to appeal to younger generations of would-be fans.

It's the most popular rumor buzzing right now: Do Oba Femi and Bronson Reed have real beef? According to WrestleVotes (h/t Knight ), some backstage in WWE aren't thrilled about the interaction on Raw this past week when Femi reacted violently to Reed putting a boot on him at the end of a segment.

Talk about storyline-bait. WWE is as scripted as it gets these days, so it's hard to imagine this was unplanned. Either way, there's now a blurred-lines effect perplexing fans as the foundation for a great main-event feud has been set.

Come on. Even if this wasn't planned, WWE has a million different ways to frame this and make it fun (Oba was using his last gasp of fight to stop the disrespect!). Any random number of people backstage could have been "surprised" by the events. It's a money start to a feud, regardless, and no doubt WWE knows it.

articles.title: WWE Just Accidentally Fell Into a Juicy Storyline
articles.summary: The best pro wrestling stories tend to just pop up organically in the moment, with bonus points if a promotion's proverbial back is against the wall.
articles.body:
The best pro wrestling stories tend to just pop up organically in the moment, with bonus points if a promotion's proverbial back is against the wall.

Lo and behold, here comes WWE with a new must-do Oba Femi storyline falling right into the laps of creative.

By now, fans know the drill. There was an already-infamous "is it real or not?" moment on the latest episode of Raw.

There, Bronson Reed made his long-anticipated return to get in the mix with some big names and, as the show came to a close, Femi was very not happy about a certain action:

Onlookers were right to point out that Femi did this stepping-on-the-defeated-guy thing to Brock Lesnar as part of his major push. Probably not something WWE wants happening to Femi on a random episode of Raw, no matter how hyped the return of Reed might be.

Unless …this is meant to drive a feud. Because the alternative is Femi actually stopped selling a beatdown momentarily to get a foot off of him. Who would be in the wrong here is pretty hard to say, all things considered.

And here's the kicker: It doesn't matter.

This could be a purposeful setup for another silly "WWE Unreal" totally-not-scripted-guys moment and it wouldn't matter.

What matters is that WWE has another hot storyline now. Before this, there were some questions of how WWE could keep Femi hot through the end of the year and all the way up to next WrestleMania, where a date with Roman Reigns seems to await.

For now, Femi has been knee-deep in a great feud with Bron Breakker. It's fantastic stuff, really, because it leans so hard into the idea that, due to some untimely injuries and poor booking, Breakker fell out of his "next big thing" spot and Femi swooped in and stole it.

But Femi-Breakker can't go on forever, assuming it continues and whatnot. Setting up Reed as his next opponent is a no-brainer because it's a must-see matchup and, really, Reed isn't going to take a lot of damage in a loss while undoubtedly looking good the whole time. His looking strong against Femi would, in a way, sort of be giving him a rub from Lesnar, too.

All that was missing was a compelling reason for Reed and Femi to feud. WWE could have been lazy (and maybe was on track before a real stepping-on incident?) and just done "big guys fight now" sort of thing between the two. But this is so much better.

How often do wrestlers get this sort of real heat these days? That blurred-lines stuff? Many attempts fail. Remember The Rock and Roman Reigns randomly complaining about insults hurled at a family tree? Silly.

The real heat these days is hard to judge. It's why, given the historical context, so much of CM Punk's stuff since he returned is classic. That blood feud with Drew McIntyre? They really hate each other, right? Seth Rollins? Kevin Owens' well-known distaste for him? Hard to get a read on.

So here we are. Did Femi really take issue with what Reed did, something that only Lesnar has been able to do? Or did Reed go into business for himself? Are people backstage really mad at one guy or the other over this, and how will it impact their future plans?

The reality? Easy money is on WWE scripting this and trying to sell the idea that Femi was still pridefully fighting with whatever he had left. But the overreactions left and right to this whole thing have made it so much more than they intended.

So much so, in fact, that we might've just been heading for tag matches and faction wars. Instead, WWE needs to correct course for a banger of a main-event feud between two fast-risers.

Good problem to have, that. Femi and Reed now have real-heat beef that fans can't get enough of, which means the promos and meetings and matches will heat up what could have otherwise been a pretty quiet part of the pro wrestling calendar to close the year.

articles.title: Sami Zayn Breaks Down in Tears After Surprise WWE Title Win vs. CM Punk in Emotional Video
articles.summary: Sami Zayn finally got justice.
articles.body:
The underdog from the underground broke down in tears after beating CM Punk to win the undisputed WWE championship on Friday Night SmackDown.

The match was set up after Punk challenged Zayn last week after Punk successfully retained his title against Johnny Gargano.

In a chaotic finishing sequence on Friday night, Gargano and Candice LeRae interfered on Zayn's behalf. Kevin Owens then ran in and attempted to hit Zayn with the title belt, but decked Punk when his former tag partner ducked.

Zayn was able to hit Owens with a low blow to get him out of the way, then nailed Punk with the helluva kick to get the pinfall. It's perhaps notable than Owens gave a wry little smile after "accidentally" hitting Punk given their issues since KO returned at SummerSlam.

The victory marks Zayn's second undisputed WWE title win. His first reign lasted just nine days when he defeated Cody Rhodes and Gunther in a triple-threat match at Night of Champions, then lost to Punk on the July 6 episode of Raw.

articles.title: Michael La Sasso’s next chapter: Her journey from NCAA champion to youngest LIV Golf winner takes another turn as he seeks a new path amid the league’s restructuring
articles.summary: International Sports News: Discover Michael La Sasso’s journey from winning the NCAA Division I championship to becoming the youngest winner in LIV Golf history. Explore his future plans as he navigates the changing landscape of professional golf.
articles.body: Michael La Sasso’s pro golf career has been on a breakneck pace. The 22-year-old, just months out of college after winning the NCAA Division I individual championship, claimed a breakthrough win at LIV Golf Indianapolis and became the youngest winner in the league’s history. The result transformed a tough season into a career-defining moment, and delivered a huge financial boost.But the timing of the victory has added another layer to La Sasso’s tale. LIV Golf is now experiencing a time of great uncertainty, and the players are being forced to consider what the next stage of their careers could look like. Instead of putting all her eggs in one tour basket, La Sasso has started looking for opportunities elsewhere, including the DP World Tour Qualifying School.Why is Michael La Sasso leaving LIV Golf?LIV Golf is undergoing major changes, a situation that prompted Michael La Sasso to seek another route. His Indianapolis victory came at a time when the future shape of the league, its financial model and player situations, was becoming less and less certain. For a young professional still building his global reputation, though, it can be especially important to keep other options open.La Sasso’s case is also unique, as his breakthrough came after a rough stretch of the LIV Golf season. He was stuck in the middle of the pack in the season standings, and before Indianapolis he was flirting with relegation. That outlook changed almost immediately with a spectacular performance that earned him his first professional title and lifted him away from the immediate danger zone.StageKey development2025Won the NCAA Division I individual championship with Ole MissJanuary 2026Left college early and joined LIV Golf’s HyFlyers GCAugust 2026Won LIV Golf IndianapolisAge 22Became the youngest LIV Golf winnerSeptember 2026Entered DP World Tour Qualifying SchoolTherefore his decision to play DP World Tour Qualifying School is more than just a change of direction. It allows La Sasso to pursue an established playing status outside the LIV ecosystem while still getting experience against an international field. It also shows the rapid changes occurring in the professional golf world for the next generation of players.Michael La Sasso leaves college and makes LIV Golf historyLa Sasso’s decision to leave college came after one of the best possible endings to his amateur career. He made history by representing the University of Mississippi and winning the 2025 NCAA Division I individual championship, cementing his legacy in college golf and earning a spot at the Masters.La Sasso decided to go pro instead of returning for his senior season. That move demonstrated faith in his game, but it also cost him the Masters opportunity that came with his amateur championship. His priority was to get himself into the professional ranks as soon as possible.La Sasso joined Phil Mickelson’s HyFlyers GC in LIV Golf in January 2026. The move put him on one of the most prominent professional golf stages and allowed him to compete against established international stars.PositionPlayerScore1stMichael La Sasso18-under2ndJon Rahm17-under3rdBryson DeChambeau16-underHis rookie season was a mixed bag initially, but Indianapolis changed all that. The win proved that, considering that she was one of the youngest players in the field, La Sasso could hang with some of the biggest names in the sport.Michael La Sasso’s journey from NCAA champion to youngest LIV Golf winnerThe Indianapolis tournament was the defining chapter of La Sasso’s first professional season. Coming into the event under a lot of pressure because of his place in the LIV Golf standings, he had an extraordinary second round that immediately changed the complexion of the tournament.La Sasso shot a second-round 10-under 60 to firmly put himself into the mix. He followed that up with another solid final round to finish the tournament at 18-under par and win by a stroke over Jon Rahm.It was a historic victory as La Sasso became the youngest player to win a LIV Golf individual title. Just 22, he beat one of the most successful players in the field and scored the biggest result of his young pro career.It was also financially rewarding. La Sasso reportedly made $2 million for the win, although the prize was less than LIV Golf’s usual individual winner’s payout, as the league continues to reevaluate its financial structure.Michael La Sasso’s next chapterLa Sasso's next task is to translate that breakthrough into sustained pro success. Winning once can create a reputation, but to maintain status across different tours requires consistency, ranking points and regular access to strong international competition.This is where his DP World Tour Qualifying School participation comes into play. La Sasso’s entry in the qualifying process shortly after his LIV Golf win shows he has his sights on more than one tournament or league.It’s a tough test, especially for someone coming out of college golf. It’s a matter of players going through stages and playing under pressure against other players trying to do the same thing with limited opportunities.But for La Sasso, the possible payoff goes beyond the immediate membership in the tour. Another recognised pathway could open the door to events across Europe and other international markets, helping him develop his game and professional profile.Perhaps the most important development for La Sasso, however, may ultimately be the willingness to keep multiple doors open. His NCAA success proved he could win at the amateur level; Indianapolis showed he could beat elite professional competition. Now, seeking DP World Tour status gives him another opportunity to test it.He's only 22 and has plenty of time to develop his career. The Indianapolis win has already given La Sasso a historic milestone, but his next decisions could be just as, if not more, important. articles.title: Coco Gauff’s former coach stunned by what US Open fans did after her match with Elena Rybakina, ‘I was really shocked’
articles.summary: Coco Gauff was unable to take advantage of the fan support she had against Elena Rybakina. Gauff was beaten by Rybakina in the US Open...
articles.body:
Coco Gauff was unable to take advantage of the fan support she had against Elena Rybakina.

Gauff was beaten by Rybakina in the US Open semi-finals, despite winning the first set of their match.

This was in spite of the loud crowd support the American received, as Rybakina commented on Gauff's fanbase after winning the match.

Gauff's former coach, Brad Gilbert , has also reacted to this, calling out some of the US Open fans for being disrespectful to Rybakina after the match.

Brad Gilbert criticises US Open fans for what they did after Coco Gauff's loss to Elena Rybakina

As with all matches on show courts like Arthur Ashe Stadium, the winning player conducts a post-match interview.

This was the case again for Rybakina, but there were very few fans still in the stadium as she spoke about the match, as many had left after she beat Gauff.

Gilbert and WTA player Ajla Tomljanovic spoke about this on The Big T Podcast , calling it both disrespectful and shocking.

Gilbert: "Can we give a yellow card to the crowd?

Gilbert: "Even though it was 99.9 for Coco, which was great, but by the time that she got to the microphone. From match point, how long do you think it was before she got to the microphone? 90 seconds."

Tomljanovic: "It's never really more than two minutes. She probably wanted to get out of there, she probably didn't take too long. And to see people leave, it's just a bit disrespectful."

Gilbert: "By the time the interview was over, the stadium was empty. It was like everyone's got a train to catch or whatever, it was like come on give her a little respect. It was a little odd how much of a mass exodus, obviously they were pretty bummed because both Americans lost, but it was only 11 o'clock at night, it wasn't three o'clock in the morning. I was really shocked."

Tomljanovic: "Especially as that's the new number one, the disrespect was a little too loud for me. And Coco herself said in her post-match interview that the crowd was 99.9% for her. You never see an American say it is that much for her, even though we all know it was."

Brad Gilbert explains what went wrong for Coco Gauff vs Elena Rybakina

Gilbert, who helped Gauff win her first Grand Slam title at the US Open in 2023, also spoke about the match itself.

Gauff was able to keep new world number one Rybakina at bay during the first set, but Gilbert highlighted the issues she was having with her forehand in the second and third sets, which her opponent took advantage of.

"I felt like in the first set, she [Rybakina] was pretty even when they showed the ball chart between going to forehand and backhand," said Gilbert. "But she was trying to force. When Coco gets forced, she gets the wheels going, she can redirect and she gets a lot more racket head speed.

"It looked like in the second and third set, a ton of balls were going down the middle and to the forehand hip where Coco then struggles with some racket head speed and she gave a lot of unforced errors. You know when she's starting to get a little bit not confident, she starts chipping the forehand a little bit.

"So I did feel like that adjustment came. I wonder if that came from her [Rybakina's] coach or was something that she saw and something that she picked up a lot. She didn't win a lot of free points on her serve in the first set and I thought the serve was much more accurate in the second and third set."

Rybakina had never been past the fourth round of the US Open before, but she is now just one win away from her third Grand Slam title.

In the women's singles final, Rybakina will play Aryna Sabalenka , who is hoping to win her third consecutive US Open title this year.

articles.title: Noah Kim Leads Former Spartans Back to Spartan Stadium
articles.summary: Noah Kim walks back into Spartan Stadium Saturday with three more former Spartans at his side. #GoGreen
articles.body:
Michigan State vs Eastern Michigan is the Spartans ' second MAC opponent in a row, but this one brings some familiar faces back to East Lansing. The Eagles carry four former Spartans, according to The Detroit News , including three projected starters: quarterback Noah Kim , guard Cole Dellinger and cornerback Caleb Coley.

Michigan State vs Eastern Michigan Game Info

Kickoff: Saturday, Sept. 12, 3:30 p.m. ET

Expectations: A high-scoring game with MSU potentially going for longer plays, after lacking them last week

What To Expect: Different Defense, Different Opportunities

MSU quarterback Alessio Milivojevic mentioned that one reason the Spartans lacked deep passing plays against Toledo was that the Rockets kept their safeties high. Eastern Michigan will give Milivojevic different looks, potentially opening up the option to go deep.

If longer plays become an option, it could help the Spartans turn field goals into touchdowns. In last week's game, MSU struggled once past midfield, settling for six field-goal attempts and just two touchdowns.

MSU head coach Pat Fitzgerald challenged his players who didn't get playing time last week to earn it in practice. Players can't take practice easy; they need to try like it's game time. If someone is making mistakes during practice, why wouldn't they in a real game?

A group likely to see change is the special teams unit. He called them out for not being physical enough and failing to execute the details in snaps. This likely came after the unit allowed Liam Boyd's 54-yard attempt to be blocked, which ended as his only miss of the game.

Eastern Michigan quarterback Noah Kim returns to Spartan Stadium for the first time since Sept. 23, 2023, when he started against Maryland. Kim left MSU after being benched partway through 2023, after throwing one touchdown and six interceptions in his final three starts. His season also coincided with the turmoil of the Mel Tucker scandal.

This game should be an "easy" win for MSU. Eastern Michigan is the lowest-rated opponent the Spartans will face all season according to CBS Sports' 136-team rankings updated Sept. 9 , which slot the Eagles 124th and the Spartans 70th. Eastern Michigan has also struggled the past few years, failing to get a winning record in MAC play in the past three seasons.

While Fitzgerald is still likely to make sure no mistakes happen due to play calling, expect more risks to be taken compared to last week. This team has an extra week under its belt, and Eastern Michigan is considered worse than Toledo. Expect to see some longer throws and fewer stalled drives for the Spartans.

Our Pick: Spartans 34 – Eastern Michigan 13

articles.title: Anna Nordqvist comments on Charley Hull and Lottie Woad Solheim Cup pairing after day one woes
articles.summary: European captain Anna Nordqvist put Charley Hull and Lottie Woad out together as the first pairing on Friday at the Solheim Cup. Hull and Woad struggled badl...
articles.body:
European captain Anna Nordqvist put Charley Hull and Lottie Woad out together as the first pairing on Friday at the Solheim Cup.

Hull and Woad struggled badly and lost 4&3 to Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz before halving their afternoon four-ball match against Yealimi Noh and Angel Yin.

The scores were tied at 4-4 after the first day's play in the Netherlands.

And Charley Hull and Lottie Woad were the worst performing duo on day one of the Solheim Cup .

Hull praised Woad's game at the Solheim Cup on Friday, but they lacked the kind of chemistry required to succeed in team competition.

Now European captain Nordqvist has responded to criticism she has received for sticking with the pairing.

Anna Nordqvist comments on Charley Hull and Lottie Woad Solheim Cup pairing

Nordqvist spoke to reporters after Hull and Woad took just 0.5 points from their two matches on Friday.

She responded when asked what her thinking was behind sticking with the duo.

" Yeah, I mean, like I said, foursome is a hard format, and I think the way this course sets up, I mean, there's quite a bit of difference who has the approach shots and iron shots, " she said.

" I think Lottie said that on hole 15, she really only had hit, like, two or three shots in the last maybe two hours.

" So foursome has always been the hardest format because it's really hard to get into pace and a rhythm. It was really cold this morning, the wind. So, yeah, like, it just takes a little bit of time, I feel like, to get in a rhythm.

" But they were also playing world No. 1, Nelly Korda, and Corpuz, who we know is a very strong pairing and they play really good. So I think that's the beauty with match play, right?

" Like, you can play good and the other team just plays better. But they fought hard, and I'm proud that we put out that pairing, and I think it's a very strong pairing for us. "

Those comments from Nordqvist simply do not ring true.

Sure, one team can play better than the other, but chemistry between two players is hugely important, and it cannot be disregarded.

Keegan Bradley made the same mistake by pairing Collin Morikawa and Harris English together on day one of the Ryder Cup last year.

It seems like Anna Nordqvist was too stubborn to make the change that quite clearly needed to be made.

Team Europe's hopes of winning the Solheim Cup will undoubtedly be affected as a result.

articles.title: ‘The squad is better than last year’s’ – Hansi Flick singles out Barcelona star who is ‘playing at a different level’
articles.summary: The coach is excited about what he’s seeing
articles.body:
Like all Barcelona fans, Hansi Flick is very excited about the team's start to the season with five wins from five games in all competitions and a very high level of performance, especially in attack.

The depth of Barça's squad is the most exciting part of the great start, with the coach able to call upon several players in all positions who can maintain the team's level even as Flick changes the side from game to game.

Hansi was asked at a press conference on Saturday about the depth of the squad compared to last season, and the boss confirmed he feels this group is stronger and also gave special praise to Pau Cubarsí, who has carried his fantastic World Cup form into the new campaign.

"The squad is better than last year's. We talk a lot about the attack, because they score a lot of goals, but for me, the defense is very important. And I see that everyone is performing at a fantastic level. After the World Cup, Cubarsi is playing at a different level. I'm very happy. He has confidence and is focused on his body. He has improved physically, especially for his position. He's playing fantastically with the ball, whether alongside Christensen or Gerard. We've done a fantastic job."

Cubarsí has indeed been a level above last season and does look stronger in one-on-one duels since the World Cup, and he seems to get better every game as he gains more experience.

And Flick is right that this season's squad looks better than last year. It feels like there are more quality options in every position, and the group fits perfectly together and is playing at a crazy level to begin the campaign.

Ups and downs will happen, but if the coach feels this strongly about his squad, we should too.

Samuel Gene Maghett (February 14, 1937 – December 1, 1969), known as Magic Sam , was an American Chicago blues musician. He was born in Grenada County, Mississippi , and learned to play the blues from listening to records by Muddy Waters and Little Walter . After moving to Chicago at the age of 19, he was signed by Cobra Records and became well known as a bluesman. He was known for his distinctive tremolo guitar playing.

Maghett moved to Chicago in 1956, where his guitar playing earned him bookings at blues clubs on the West Side. He recorded singles for Cobra Records from 1957 to 1959, including "All Your Love" and "Easy Baby". They did not reach the record charts but had a profound influence, far beyond Chicago's guitarists and singers. Together with recordings by Otis Rush and Buddy Guy (also Cobra artists), the West Side Sound was a manifesto for a new kind of blues. Around this time Magic Sam worked briefly with Homesick James Williamson . Magic Sam gained a following before being drafted into the U.S. Army. He served six months in prison for desertion and received a dishonorable discharge .
