articles.title: Dodgers Post Argues Shohei Ohtani’s Season-Ending Injury, ‘He’s Done’
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ two-way superstar is “done for the season,” argued one prominent voice around the team.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have gradually reduced Shohei Ohtani 's workload as his injury problems have continued to mount, creating increasing uncertainty about what the two-way superstar will be able to contribute during the final weeks of the regular season or in the playoffs.

Ohtani has already been dealing with multiple physical issues, and the Dodgers have become increasingly cautious with his pitching responsibilities. The latest development has raised questions about whether the team will ultimately shut him down altogether, even as it continues to leave open the possibility of a postseason return.

"He has battled through multiple physical limitations throughout the year, including left knee inflammation and right biceps soreness that limited him to 14 starts and 85 2/3 innings as a pitcher and has now sidelined him completely," Katie Woo reported for The Athletic . "It is all but official he won't pitch again this season. It is unknown what he'll be able to provide as a hitter."

That uncertainty has fueled even more speculation surrounding Ohtani's status, particularly with the Dodgers seemingly prioritizing his long-term health over his availability during the regular season and perhaps pushing him too far.

Los Angeles Dodgers Superstar Shohei Ohtani Seen As 'Done For The Season'

On the "Dodgers Post," the California's Post's prominent podcast hosted by beat reporters Dylan Hernandez and Jack Harris, a debate over whether Ohtani would return at all this year was raised.

"He's done for the season," Hernandez said on the latest episode . "(The Dodgers) are just pretending he's not. He's done for, like, all intents and purposes."

The Dodgers have demonstrated a willingness to exercise caution with their other prominent pitchers, including Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow . But shutting down Ohtani at this point, as the team pursues its third straight championship, would be a major surprise.

Los Angeles Dodgers' Shohei Ohtani Season Ending Decision Debated

While Hernandez believes Ohtani's regular season could effectively be finished, his co-host argued a more optimistic view of his postseason availability.

"I think it's possible he doesn't play in the regular season," Harris said on the episode. "There's no chance he's not going to play in the playoffs."

For their part, the Dodgers have suggested Ohtani could stay off the mound for the rest of the year, but they haven't indicated he could miss the playoffs. Hernandez, however, warned fans against relying too heavily on the Dodgers' public messaging.

"The Dodgers have proven themselves to be horrible sources of information regarding Ohtani," Hernandez added. "So, don't listen to anything that they say. Use your eyes."

For now, fans' eyes will show a Dodgers star whose workload has steadily diminished as his physical problems have grown.

articles.title: There may not be much Ohtani to see when Giants face the Dodgers in final weeks
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Dodgers aren't able to count on Shohei Ohtani to save them as they risk falling in among the NL wild cards. Can the San Francisco Giants make...
articles.body:
Baseball's best team is going to see a lot of the San Francisco Giants during these final days of the regular season. Given that it's a brave new world around here, we'll make sure all of them get a proper introduction.

The Los Angeles Dodgers couldn't possibly know much about Jonah Cox, Turner Hill, Shay Whitcomb , Drew Cavanaugh, Trent Harris - there, that covers about half the group. The defending champs are too busy trying to figure out their postseason plans, and it's a lot more complicated than you may think.

The Dodgers without Shohei Ohtani ? Unthinkable.

Resting uncomfortably on the injured list, felled by a sore left knee and right arm, Ohtani won't be in uniform for the Giants ' three-game series that begins Friday at Dodger Stadium. When the two teams close out the season at Oracle Park on Sept. 25-27, he will have been eligible for only two prior games, against San Diego at home.

Until recently, the Dodgers tried to shake off Ohtani's aches and pains. This is the greatest talent in the history of baseball, a man who looks damn near indestructible at times. He rises above everyone, godlike, as he lodges a three-run homer alongside a pitching masterpiece.

But these are significant injuries. The left knee is his landing leg as he strides off the mound, and that can't be a "sort of" recovery. Adding the element of a constantly sore biceps, Ohtani hasn't pitched since July 3 - and now there's no chance he takes that risk until the postseason.

Nobody's counting on that. For one thing, the Dodgers have a rock-solid rotation that would run four deep in October: Yoshinobu Yamamoto , Tarik Skubal , Blake Snell (looking just about unhittable since he got back on the mound) and Tyler Glasnow .

Ohtani could be kind of a cool choice to pitch some emergency relief in October - he's done it before - and it's possible that if the Dodgers avoid having to play a wild-card round, he will have had enough time to get the arm back in shape. That hardly seems likely, though. The Dodgers were in denial about the extent of Ohtani's injuries (they're openly wishing now they'd put him on the IL a month earlier), and he's kind of a wreck right now, admitting, "I think I want to focus on offense."

That's a troubling issue, as well. He's gone a sorrowful 6-for-49 since his last home run (Aug. 18), and as much as the prideful Ohtani hates to reveal even the slightest vulnerability, he has often appeared to be in significant pain swinging the bat.

For the Giants, that final weekend carries untold promise. They could knock the Dodgers into the wild-card round, depending on how Atlanta and Milwaukee fare down the stretch. Then again, L.A. would like to believe Ohtani puts the whole mess behind him, stunning the Oracle crowd with titanic blasts into the bay.

The 3-Dot doesn't quite see it that way. We'll say the heroes in that series will be named Molina, Basabe, Knizner and Furman. Just as we knew all along.

There are things about Bryce Eldridge - the technique, the patience, the confidence, the big moments - that suggest he'll fit into a fine Giants tradition. As far back as you'd like to go, this franchise is a haven for power-hitting lefty first basemen.

Hall of Famers abound, from 19th-century star Roger Connor to Bill Terry, Johnny Mize and Willie McCovey. Will Clark should be in Cooperstown, and there's always hope.

Longtime mainstay Whitey Lockman showed a measure of power for the New York teams of the 1950s. Darrell Evans mostly played third base in San Francisco , but he slugged 30 homers and made the All-Star team as a first baseman in 1983. Save a special place for J.T. Snow, who became strictly a lefty hitter (no longer switch hitting) mid-career and hit some very important home runs.

I would include Bill White, a first-rate prospect who broke with the 1956 Giants and had a fine season, counting Robin Roberts and Don Newcombe among his 22-homer victims, then went into the military service. Not much had changed upon his return, other than the Giants had moved to San Francisco and the position was suddenly loaded with Orlando Cepeda and the fast-rising McCovey. (White was dealt to St. Louis in 1959 and started for the '64 world champs.)

Nobody's forgetting Brandon Belt in this discussion, and the way Rafael Devers is hitting, he'll be in the mythical team photo. Right along with "Late Night" LaMonte Wade and Travis Ishikawa , who gets there with a single swing.

As this is written, the U.S. team and France are on course to meet in Sunday's final of the FIBA women's basketball World Cup. Interesting that the two have switched places in the latest FIBA world rankings, with France now ranked No. 1, and this is no surprise. With Gabby Williams and fellow WNBA standout Leila Lacan (Connecticut) in the starting lineup, I defy anyone to find a better backcourt bench than Marine Johannes, Carla Leite, Pauline Astier and the Valkyries ' Janelle Salaün (who plays on the wing) in the history of women's international play - non-USA division.

They're calling Johannes a "circus act" now, in the most delightful context. Some of her off-hand bullet passes must be re-watched to confirm the reality. She can hit any kind of drive shot in traffic with either hand, and she has a Stephen Curry -like array of trickery. In a dead-ball moment Thursday against China, she got the ball in the far right corner, looked directly at midcourt and swished the shot without a glance.

Johannes is a beacon of deferential grace, as such drawing absolutely no attention to herself. After a while, though, you realize you've never seen a player with such an artistic array of long-range shots, at times drifting far to her left or shooting off one leg, just for the heck of it.

On the other side of the court in this dream final, Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese are finding harmony as a formidable pair: Reese the greatest rebounder in WNBA history and Clark back to peak performance as a magnificent passer and outside (way outside) shooter. Their feud was never the violent or stare-down kind, but they seemed a bit dismissive of each other until now, as teammates. And they're finding it quite the kick.

• Final WNBA note, as relayed by si.com: A complicated formula known as Regularized Adjusted Plus-Minus (RAPM) takes into account ball security, playmaking, assist-to-turnover ratio, shot accuracy, getting to the free-throw line, and defense broken down to specific opponents. And who emerges as the league's Most Impactful Player , based on statistics right up to the World Cup break? The Valkyries' Veronica Burton . Good call, for she's all of that.

There was widespread celebration and relief in Bay Area circles when KNBR reinstated Greg Papa. There was lingering resentment, as well. It's great to know that Papa will have regular "Lunch With Papa" and "Niners Update" segments on the station, and that he seems very much on course to be calling 49ers games again. But it's hard to forget the incomprehensibly cruel nature of KNBR's decision to dismiss a legendary broadcaster undergoing life-threatening hospitalization and taking a severe financial hit.

The KNBR people offered no explanation, just a bunch of meaningless words. Sources say it had to be a "cost-cutting move," and that's oddly fitting. This cut came with massive cost.

articles.title: Andrew Whitworth expects another big season from the Broncos
articles.summary: "Denver is going to be the team in the AFC," Andrew Whitworth said of the Broncos.
articles.body:
In a recent appearance on the Rich Eisen Show, former All-Pro and current Thursday Night Football analyst Andrew Whitworth said the Denver Broncos are on an upward trajectory heading into 2026

Whitworth acknowledged what could have been in the 2025 Super Bowl, while looking forward to Denver's 2026 season, especially against the Seattle Seahawks , a game which Whitworth will attend as part of the TNF crew.

"That's another one," Whitworth said of the Broncos - Seahawks matchup in Week 6. "I still think that's a game that could have been last year's Super Bowl, but it also could be this year's. Both those teams have the potential to be there again."

The big game against Seattle will be a pivotal one for the Broncos ; it is the final game of a brutal six-game opening stretch ; however, it will be potentially the best-looking game of the season , as both squads will wear their beautiful throwback uniforms.

Whitworth complimented the Broncos for their moves in the 2026 offseason, showing they can be contenders once again.

"Denver to me is another one that I just think they've made some moves that I think are going to make them a little more explosive on offense," Whitworth said. "I'm looking for that defense to kind of return and be even if they're not as elite as they were last year, they're still going to be really, really good. I think that this team right there, Denver is going to be the team in the AFC. I just have a feeling they're going to be one of those teams at the end that you're going to be dealing with again."

You can view Whitworth's full comments below.

The Broncos begin their season in an extremely tough environment, at Arrowhead Stadium against the Kansas City Chiefs in their first primetime game of the season. Can the Broncos prove they are once again contenders? Or was last year a fluke? We'll soon find out.

articles.title: New Orleans Saints vs. Detroit Lions Week 1 preview: 3 key stats
articles.summary: A data-driven preview of Saints at Lions, focusing on key stats and matchups.
articles.body:
As enjoyable as NFL free agency, the NFL Draft, organized team activities, training camp, preseason, and 53-man roster coverage can be, nothing beats an NFL Sunday—and Week 1 is one of the most fulfilling and anticipated days of the year.

The Detroit Lions need this Week 1. They need it to wash away the ghosts of last year's opener and fully bury the disappointment of last season for everyone in the organization and the fan base. And to get back to playing Dan Campbell football, the Lions will take on the team that helped cultivate Campbell into the coach he eventually became in Detroit.

The New Orleans Saints entered last season much like the narrative surrounding the 2026 Arizona Cardinals : written off and considered a favorite to land the first overall pick in the NFL Draft. But New Orleans' season became a tale of two halves. The Saints were a plucky bunch that started 1-8 before finishing on a 5-3 tear.

That makes them a potentially dangerous Week 1 opponent—a team with a decent roster and coaching staff entering Year 2 that has built some belief in itself. That's something Lions fans should be plenty familiar with.

Below are my three key stats and matchups for the Lions' season and home opener.

Note: Unless otherwise indicated, all statistics are sourced from NFL Pro, FTN Fantasy, Pro Football Reference, or Pro Football Focus.

A strong finish to one season doesn't always translate to a team immediately picking up where it left off the next. But without any in-season evidence yet, it's our best sample to judge what once-heralded defensive mind Brandon Staley's defensive demons might be trotting out at Ford Field—even with the offseason losses of Deario Davis and Alontae Taylor , along with future Saints Ring of Honor member Cameron Jordan already ruled out.

From Weeks 10-18 last season, the Saints finished top 10 in defensive DVOA and top five in passing EPA, rushing EPA, passing success rate, and rushing success rate allowed—including an absurdly low 39.2% offensive passing success rate.

During that span, edge rusher Chase Young spent 98.9% of his snaps lined up on the defensive right side, while Carl Granderson spent 88% of his snaps on the defensive left. Young's 36 total quarterback pressures ranked tied for 11th among all defenders, even with Micah Parsons , while Granderson's pass-rush win rate jumped from 8.0% early in the season to 12.3%.

Even with the addition of Tyree Wilson , there will likely be a steady dose of Young against Penei Sewell and Granderson against rookie Blake Miller . That's two formidable foes for the Lions' newly entrenched bookends to kick off the season.

Kool-Aid McKinstry also became a completely different player during the second half of the season. After allowing a 120.0 passer rating, 68.1% reception rate, six touchdowns, and committing five penalties early in the year, those numbers plummeted to a 73.3 passer rating, 45.9% reception rate, two touchdowns, and zero penalties over the second half. McKinstry will enter his third season with confidence as the Saints' CB1.

Also notably, linebacker Pete Werner improved from a 50.4 PFF defensive grade in the first half to 67.6 in the second. New third linebacker on the depth chart Danny Stutsman played 147 of his 204 season snaps during the second half and raised his PFF defensive grade from 59.8 to 74.3.

Then-rookie safety and now nickelback Jonas Sanker experienced a similar surge, with his run-defense grade climbing from 63.6 to 78.1, which ranked 13th among 67 qualifying safeties from Weeks 10-18.

It's a relatively young defense that began to coalesce within Staley's system down the stretch and is now being further entrusted to develop into a unit capable of helping guide New Orleans back to the postseason. This is a solid, ascending defense that will challenge the Lions and new offensive coordinator Drew Petzing immediately, providing a proper Week 1 litmus test for whether Detroit's offense can get back to being a consistently dominant unit.

Stalwart Saints linebacker Demario Davis returned to the New York Jets for his third stint there after a wildly successful eight seasons in New Orleans. Replacing him is a Saints boomerang and the son of former Lions standout Luther Elliss, Kaden Elliss , who will play on the second level alongside Pete Werner and Danny Stutsman.

Elliss is one of the most disruptive pass-rushing off-ball linebackers in football, averaging 7.9 pass-rush reps per game over the last four seasons. During that span, Elliss has combined for 19.5 sacks and 42 quarterback hits—as many QB hits as Cameron Jordan—which rank second and first, respectively, among all off-ball linebackers.

Last season, Elliss recorded an 18.3% pass-rush win rate, fifth among off-ball linebackers, along with an impressive 17.6% pressure rate. That came one season after he generated a 21.5% pressure rate in 2024, which ranked seventh among off-ball linebackers.

Elliss is a one-man demolition crew as a pass-rushing linebacker up the middle. With Bryan Bresee out for the season and the Saints' remaining defensive tackle group largely unproven or lackluster, Elliss and his attack-mode aggression will provide the toughest test for the Lions' gelling interior offensive line of new center Juice Scruggs , third-year left guard Christian Mahogany (and possibly Ben Bartch ), and second-year right guard Tate Ratledge .

Their communication and chemistry in the middle will be key to preventing Elliss from single-handedly submarining a Lions drive or two.

The two highest-rated recruits in Oregon's 2018 recruiting class were Lions sixth-year left tackle Penei Sewell and Saints second-year quarterback Tyler Shough , with Shough intended to be the eventual heir apparent to Justin Herbert . Not everything went according to plan there. However, the Saints' decision to take Shough early in the second round last year did, as the signal-caller positioned himself to potentially be their long-term answer after taking over as the starter in Week 9 and holding the job through the final nine games.

During that span, Shough ranked tied for third with a 69.2% completion percentage, ninth at 7.6 yards per attempt, and ninth with a 95.8 passer rating. Those are impressive top-10 metrics for a rookie quarterback in Year 1 of Kellen Moore's system.

Not only were the Saints the fastest-paced offense in football last season, averaging just 27 seconds between snaps, but Shough also made quick decisions with the football once he became the starter. His 2.71-second average time to throw was the fourth-fastest in the NFL, with Jared Goff ranking first.

Shough was particularly successful targeting players out of the slot, with his leading targets there going to Juwan Johnson (28), Chris Olave (24), and DeVaughn Vele (12). On throws to the slot, Shough ranked top 10 in passer rating (10th, 104.6), yards per attempt (sixth, 8.8), completion percentage (fourth, 74.5%), and, most impressively, EPA per dropback (fourth, 0.45) among 33 qualifying quarterbacks.

Defending targets to the slot is one of the biggest mysteries for the Lions. Those matchups will likely involve some combination of Christian Izien ( questionable ) and Day 3 rookie Keith Abney II at nickelback, along with still-uncertain coverage responsibilities for linebackers Jack Campbell , Derrick Barnes , Malcolm Rodriguez , and Devin White , plus safeties Chuck Clark , Avonte Maddox , and Thomas Harper .

Factoring in the communication required to defend a fast-paced offense and quick passing game that frequently attacks the slot, this will provide a much-needed early-season test for Detroit's middle-of-the-field coverage defenders.

All of that comes with one important weakness to keep in mind: Shough short-circuited under pressure. His 25.9% pressure-to-sack rate ranked 29th out of 33 qualifying quarterbacks, potentially providing an avenue for the Lions' high-upside defensive front to feast against an otherwise above-average Saints offensive line.

articles.summary: David Pollack predicts Oklahoma will beat Michigan 24-17 after questioning the Wolverines' Week 1 performance.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners vs. the Michigan Wolverines is one of the biggest games of Week 2. The Sooners started the season with a dominant 51-0 win over the University of Texas at El Paso Miners, whereas the Wolverines struggled in their 13-12 win over the Western Michigan Broncos.

Still, this game features two of the biggest brands in college football. It's also the first trip for the Sooners to Ann Arbor. The two have faced each other only twice. One was in 1976, when Oklahoma beat Michigan in the Orange Bowl to win the national championship. The other was last year, when the Sooners defeated Michigan in Norman.

College football analyst David Pollack said he feels Oklahoma will win again on Saturday.

"Oklahoma looks way better," Pollack said on 'See Ball Get Ball with David Pollack.' "There's no way I can pick Michigan after last week and what I saw in the struggles, but I do think it'll be somewhat competitive. I got it like 24-17. Oklahoma winning the football game at Michigan."

The contrast between the two teams' openers is difficult to ignore. Oklahoma scored 51 points, recorded 401 yards of total offense and shut out UTEP, while Michigan needed a controversial final sequence to avoid a stunning loss to Western Michigan.

The Wolverines' defense did keep them in the game, limiting Western Michigan to 221 yards of total offense, but the offense struggled to consistently move the football. Oklahoma, meanwhile, looked much more complete in its opener.

That doesn't mean the Sooners can overlook Michigan. The Wolverines have a talented roster, a strong defense and home-field advantage, which is why Pollack still expects the game to be competitive despite his confidence in Oklahoma.

The Sooners and Wolverines will play at 11:00 a.m. CT on Saturday on Fox.

articles.title: Nick Saban praises Oklahoma Sooners head coach Brent Venables
articles.summary: Nick Saban calls Brent Venables one of the best defensive coordinators ever
articles.body:
Oklahoma Sooners head coach Brent Venables has a strong reputation as one of the best defensive minds in college football. Venables has won three national championships as a defensive coordinator. One with Oklahoma and two with the Clemson Tigers .

Venables' defenses bring an aggressive approach, with his units consistently built around disguising coverages, creating pressure and forcing opposing offenses into difficult situations.

Legendary former Alabama Crimson Tide head coach Nick Saban faced Venables' defenses many times with the national championship on the line. He said that Venables is one of the best defensive minds the game has seen.

"I think Venables is one of the best defensive coordinators ever," Saban said on 'The Pat McAfee Show.' "I know he's a head coach now, but he's still calling the defense. He's the one guy who is so aggressive that he's always trying to put you behind the eight ball by creating negative plays on offense."

The timing of Saban's praise is particularly notable with Oklahoma preparing to face the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday. The Sooners' defense enters the matchup with the reputation, talent and experience to make life difficult for Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood .

Michigan struggled offensively in its season opener against the Western Michigan Broncos , and Oklahoma's defensive front presents a much more difficult challenge. The Sooners recorded four sacks and 10 tackles for loss in their Week 1 shutout, while Venables has already emphasized the need for his defense to become cleaner after some missed tackles and containment issues.

Saban's comments ultimately reinforce what Oklahoma has already shown: Venables' defense is designed to make an offense uncomfortable. Against Michigan, the question won't simply be whether the Sooners can make plays. It will be whether Venables can once again turn his aggressive defensive philosophy into the kind of negative plays that change the outcome of a marquee matchup.

articles.title: “Another Conspiracy Theory Proven Fact”: Caitlin Clark Fans React as Cathy Engelbert Reportedly Chose Not to Build Relation With Fever Superstar
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark fans had their “I told you so” moment on Friday after a report suggested that WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert never tried to build a relation...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark fans had their "I told you so" moment on Friday after a report suggested that WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert never tried to build a relationship with the Indiana Fever superstar.

Many of Clark's fans felt the league didn't do enough to promote her or recognize her influence in improving the WNBA's popularity.

Here's what the report from Sports Business Journal said:

"In conversations with multiple executives with ties to teams and the league, the No. 1 prerequisite for the next commissioner should be "relationship repair" and/or "relationship building" — and that is in reaction to Engelbert's perceived disconnect with coaches, GMs, players and specifically Clark herself."

The report supported the claim, noting that Cathy Engelbert has not attended an Indiana Fever game since 2024. She was scheduled to do so in August, but the trip was canceled. A league spokesperson conveyed that Engelbert declined an interview for this story.

The report added that Engelbert was cautious about avoiding any "preponderance of Caitlin Clark favoritism" as the league largely consisted of Black athletes, which, according to her critics, she took too far.

Clark's fans quickly pointed out their two years' worth of belief that Engelbert didn't do enough to build a relationship with the Fever superstar after this report surfaced.

"Another conspiracy theory proven fact," one fan wrote.

Sophie Cunningham questions why people are reluctant to credit Caitlin Clark for her impact in women's sports

Caitlin Clark's Fever teammate Sophie Cunningham questioned why people do not give the superstar point guard her flowers. On Colin Cowherd's show , the host and Cunningham broke down Clark's impact.

"I look at her and I think she's got Jordan's ascension, Curry's game, and Larry Bird's personality. Am I wrong?" Cowherd said.

Cunningham agreed with Cowherd's statement. She then elaborated on Clark's personality and what she has done for the sport.

"I think that Larry Bird honestly might have a little bit more sass," she said. "Caitlin is just her own. Her own personality. Especially off the court, she is strictly basketball. She loves to sit on the couch, she loves to watch TV, she's very simple."

Cunningham said it was a "blessing" to have Clark in the WNBA. Cunningham noted that the league has always been talented, but credited Clark with drawing attention and making people see why the WNBA is worth watching.

After mentioning these aspects, Cunningham raised the big question of Clark not getting her flowers.

"I don't know why people are so reluctant to give her her flowers," she said.

The discourse around Caitlin Clark and her influence has been prominent as she rounds off her third season in the WNBA after a few weeks. Many who believe Clark alone isn't responsible for the league's growth over the past two years blame her fans and certain media personnel for dismissing the greats before her and what they brought to the table.
